summary: Displays a start banner, opens the reference file, then loops while END-OF-FILE is 'N' reading records and displaying them before closing the file and returning.

business_rules.rule: The main control loop continues to read and display reference file records only while END-OF-FILE equals 'N'; once END-OF-FILE is set to 'Y', the loop terminates and the file is closed.
Each record read from the reference file is displayed to standard output before the loop continues to the next iteration.
The 0000-XREFFILE-OPEN procedure is executed before any read operation to ensure the reference file is open for input.
The 9000-XREFFILE-CLOSE procedure is executed after the read loop completes to release the reference file resource.

summary: Reads the next record from CARD-XREF-RECORD, evaluates XREFFILE-STATUS to set APPL-RESULT (0=success, 16=end-of-file, 12=error), and branches to either continue processing, set END-OF-FILE flag, or display status and abend.

business_rules.rule: A successful read (XREFFILE-STATUS = '00') sets APPL-RESULT to 0 (APPL-AOK) and proceeds with record processing.
An XREFFILE-STATUS value of '10' is interpreted as normal end-of-file, setting APPL-RESULT to 16 (APPL-EOF).
Any XREFFILE-STATUS value other than '00' or '10' is treated as an error, setting APPL-RESULT to 12 and triggering a display of the status code followed by an abend.

When APPL-EOF is satisfied (APPL-RESULT = 16), END-OF-FILE is set to 'Y' to signal loop termination, the status is displayed, IO-STATUS is set to XREFFILE-STATUS, and the program abends via the 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM procedure.

summary: Opens the reference file for input, checks XREFFILE-STATUS to set APPL-RESULT (0=open success, 12=open failure), and abends with a diagnostic message if the open fails.

business_rules.rule: The reference file must open successfully (XREFFILE-STATUS = '00') before any read operations can proceed; a failed open sets APPL-RESULT to 12 and triggers an abend.
On open failure, the current XREFFILE-STATUS value is moved to IO-STATUS and displayed via 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS before the program abends.

summary: Closes the reference file, checks XREFFILE-STATUS to set APPL-RESULT (0=close success, 12=close failure), and abends with a diagnostic message if the close fails.

business_rules.rule: The reference file close operation is validated; a successful close (XREFFILE-STATUS = '00') sets APPL-RESULT to 0, while any other status sets APPL-RESULT to 12.
On close failure, the XREFFILE-STATUS is moved to IO-STATUS, displayed via 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, and the program abends via 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM.

summary: Displays an abend notification message, sets TIMING to 0 and ABCODE to 999, then calls the Language Environment CEE3ABD service to force a controlled abnormal program termination.

business_rules.rule: The program always terminates with abend code 999 (set in ABCODE) and zero timing, invoked via the CEE3ABD Language Environment service for a controlled abnormal termination.

summary: Evaluates IO-STATUS to determine whether the status code is numeric or non-numeric; for non-numeric codes it decodes the value using the TWO-BYTES-BINARY/TWO-BYTES-RIGHT overlay pattern, then displays the normalised four-digit status code.

business_rules.rule: When IO-STATUS is non-numeric, the status is decoded as a VSAM extended code: IO-STAT1 is set to 1 in IO-STATUS-04, TWO-BYTES-BINARY is zeroed, IO-STAT2 is moved to TWO-BYTES-RIGHT, and the resulting TWO-BYTES-BINARY integer value is placed in IO-STATUS-0403 for display.
When IO-STATUS is numeric, IO-STATUS-04 is set to '0000' with the last two characters overlaid from IO-STATUS, and the result is displayed as a normalised four-digit status code.
